subject: FY25 Preliminary Budget Departmental Reviews
overview: The Committee of the Whole held its fourth preliminary budget hearing for fiscal year 2025 to review proposals from Human Resources, the Assessor, the Building Department, Diversity Equity and Inclusion, and the Treasurer-Collector. The council discussed the transition of pandemic-funded positions to the general fund and efforts to modernize departmental software and fee collection processes.

items.title: Human Resources, Health Insurance, and Workers' Compensation
items.summary: The department presented a $267,537 budget that moves a personnel coordinator from federal grant funding to the general fund and adds new safety and compliance training. Health insurance costs increased by $2.7 million, or 10 percent, primarily due to rising state health insurance rates.

items.title: Assessor's Department
items.summary: The Chief Assessor proposed a $586,609 budget including a part-time field assessor to meet state-mandated property review cycles and noted that the transition to a June valuation date will reduce tax adjustment lags. The department reported an estimated $2.2 million in new growth and a significant decrease in valuation appeals cases.

items.title: Building Department
items.summary: The department reviewed a $1,030,354 budget, highlighting the launch of a multi-language online permit portal and a policy shift to require permit fees be paid at the time of application to ensure collection. Discussions also covered the future digitization of paper records and the tracking of vacant storefronts and short-term rentals.

items.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI)
items.summary: The department presented a $117,552 budget that moves language access services to the general fund and prioritizes ADA coordination and federal equal opportunity compliance. The director emphasized the need for future staff expansion to handle the increasing volume of physical accessibility inspections and federal regulatory monitoring.

items.title: Treasurer-Collector's Department
items.summary: The department proposed a $755,193 budget driven by increases in postage rates and data processing services for tax billing. The Treasurer reported on recent staff certifications and noted that the city has collected over $515,000 in tax titles so far this year.
